lead: A hillside neighbourhood with a strong community, a viaduct, distinctive houses and views.
text: It grew out of the union of two old neighbourhoods, Vallcarca and els Penitents, and is one of the highest and steepest in the city. It was a summer retreat and a home for valley families looking for better connections, and in the 1970s its residents campaigned for the improvements that brought the metro, the sewers and the escalators.

Its landscape mixes the Vallcarca viaduct, the church of els Josepets, distinctive houses such as Casa Comas d'Argemir, Casa Marsans and Casa Barangé, garden-city areas such as the Torrent Maduixer, developed in 1950, and detached villas in Mas Falcó. At 4,152 €/m², its sale price is above that of El Coll and below that of the rest of Gràcia.
housing: Detached villas, garden-city housing and blocks of flats, on steeply sloping streets.
